eliu.name: Eliu
eliu.note: Son of Barachel the Buzite; the angry young bystander who speaks after the three friends fall silent.

1.t: At this my heart trembleth, and is moved out of its place.

2.t: Hear ye attentively the terror of his voice, and the sound that cometh out of his mouth.

3.t: He beholdeth under all the heavens, and his light is upon the ends of the earth.

4.t: After it a noise shall roar, he shall thunder with the voice of his majesty, and shall not be found out, when his voice shall be heard.

5.t: God shall thunder wonderfully with his voice, he that doth great and unsearchable things.

6.t: He commandeth the snow to go down upon the earth, and the winter rain, and the shower of his strength.

7.t: He sealeth up the hand of all men, that every one may know his works.

8.t: Then the beast shall go into his covert, and shall abide in his den.

9.t: Out of the inner parts shall a tempest come, and cold out of the north.

10.t: When God bloweth there cometh frost, and again the waters are poured out abundantly.

11.t: Corn desireth clouds, and the clouds spread their light:

12.t: Which go round about, whithersoever the will of him that governeth them shall lead them, to whatsoever he shall command them upon the face of the whole earth:

13.t: Whether in one tribe, or in his own land, or in what place soever of his mercy he shall command them to be found.

14.t: Hearken to these things, Job: Stand, and consider the wondrous works of God.

15.t: Dost thou know when God commanded the rains, to shew his light of his clouds?

16.t: Knowest thou the great paths of the clouds, and the perfect knowledges?

17.t: Are not thy garments hot, when the south wind blows upon the earth?

18.t: Thou perhaps hast made the heavens with him, which are most strong, as if they were of molten brass.

19.t: Shew us what we may say to him: or we are wrapped up in darkness.

20.t: Who shall tell him the things I speak? even if a man shall speak, he shall be swallowed up.

21.t: But now they see not the light: the air on a sudden shall be thickened into clouds, and the wind shall pass and drive them away.

22.t: Cold cometh out of the north, and to God praise with fear.

23.t: We cannot find him worthily: he is great in strength, and in judgment, and in justice, and he is ineffable.

24.t: Therefore men shall fear him, and all that seem to themselves to be wise, shall not dare to behold him.
